title: Cognitive & Learning Disabilities 🧠
description: Dyslexia, ADHD, memory impairments – design for clarity, consistency and focus.

slides.title: The Invisible Disabilities 🧩
slides.content:
Cognitive disabilities include:

* **Dyslexia** – difficulty reading text; may use text‑to‑speech.
* **ADHD** – easily distracted; need clean, focused layouts.
* **Memory impairments** – need reminders, consistent navigation.
* **Intellectual disabilities** – simple language, clear instructions.

These are the **largest group** of people with disabilities on the web.

quizData.question: Why might a dyslexic user prefer a site with icons alongside text?

options.text: Icons help recognition and reduce reading effort
Icons are more accessible for screen readers

quizData.explanation: Icons can provide visual cues that make content easier to recognise without relying solely on decoding text.

slides.title: Readability & Language 📖
slides.content:
* Use **plain language** – short sentences, active voice.
* Define unusual terms, avoid jargon.
* Left‑align text (for left‑to‑right languages).
* Adequate line height (1.5) and paragraph spacing.
* Avoid walls of text – use headings, lists, and whitespace.

quizData.question: Which of the following improves readability for cognitive disabilities?

options.text: Short paragraphs, clear headings, bullet points

quizData.explanation: Clear structure and short blocks help users scan and comprehend content.

slides.title: Focus & Distraction 🎯
slides.content:
Users with ADHD or autism may be overwhelmed by:

* Auto‑playing videos / animations.
* Pop‑ups and interstitials.
* Busy backgrounds with low contrast.

**Solution**: Provide a 'reduce motion' preference (prefers‑reduced‑motion), allow pausing, and keep UI predictable.

slides.title: Consistency & Navigation 🗺️
slides.content:
* Keep navigation in the same place on every page.
* Use standard icons and predictable interactions.
* Offer **multiple ways** to find content (search, menu, site map).
* Provide clear error messages with suggestions.

Cognitive accessibility = less cognitive load.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Test with Real Users

Cognitive accessibility is highly individual. Include people with cognitive disabilities in your usability testing – their feedback is priceless.
